title: Sperm whales: a possible ‘phonetic alphabet’ in their calls
summary: Analysis of nearly 9,000 codas from the eastern Caribbean clan, collected over more than ten years, proposes a combinatorial structure involving rhythm, tempo, rubato and ornamentation. Published in Nature Communications; communicative function remains unknown, data cover one clan, and the page does not specify machine-learning methods.

evidence.tested: Nearly 9,000 codas from the eastern Caribbean clan, collected over more than ten years, were analyzed for context-sensitive features (rubato, ornamentation) and categorical rhythm and tempo.
evidence.unknown: The communicative function of many codas is unknown, whether the features encode intent needs future field research, and the duality-of-patterning link is only a possibility.
evidence.ai_role: Not reported; the page does not specify what machine learning did in the analysis.
